# 12-Week Postpartum Return Programme

**Client Profile:** 33 y/o female, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, OB-cleared for light activity only until 6-week check. Training at home with a yoga mat. Goals assumed: safe return to fitness, restore core/pelvic floor function, rebuild capacity for daily life and eventual return to general training.

**Important caveats for the trainer:**
- Re-confirm OB clearance for progressive exercise at the 6-week check before moving past Phase 1.
- Screen for diastasis recti (DR) before Phase 2 and at each phase transition. If a gap >2 fingers with poor tension, hold core progressions and refer to a pelvic health physio.
- Screen for symptoms of pelvic floor dysfunction (leaking, heaviness, prolapse sensation, pain with intercourse) — refer out if present.
- Watch the C-section scar: numbness, pulling, or adhesions warrant scar mobilisation (see Phase 2).
- Sleep, breastfeeding, and stress will heavily affect recovery. Build in flexibility.

---

## PHASE 1 — Weeks 1–2 of programme (Client weeks 4–6 postpartum): Restorative Foundation

**Goal:** Re-establish breath-driven core connection, gentle mobility, walking tolerance. NO abdominal flexion, NO loaded lifting, NO impact.

**Frequency:** Daily breath/mobility work (10–15 min) + walking.

### Daily Session A — Breath & Reconnection (10–15 min)

1. **Diaphragmatic breathing, supine, knees bent** — 2 min. Hand on belly, hand on ribs. Inhale into ribs/belly 360°, exhale long and soft.
2. **Connection breath (exhale + gentle pelvic floor + TVA cue)** — 2 × 8 breaths. Inhale to expand; on exhale gently "lift" pelvic floor (cue: stopping wind) and draw lower belly toward spine. Full release on inhale.
3. **Pelvic tilts, supine** — 2 × 10 slow.
4. **Glute squeezes, supine** — 2 × 10 with 2-sec hold.
5. **Supported child's pose** — 60 sec, breathing into the back ribs.
6. **Cat–cow, all fours** — 2 × 8 slow.
7. **Side-lying thoracic openers** — 1 × 6/side.

### Walking
- Week 1: 10–15 min, 1–2× daily, flat terrain, easy pace.
- Week 2: 15–25 min, 1–2× daily.
- Stop if bleeding increases or colour returns to red — sign of overdoing it.

### Scar awareness (no mobilisation yet — wait until fully healed and OB-cleared)
- Light fingertip touch around (not on) the scar to begin desensitisation.

---

## PHASE 2 — Weeks 3–4 (Client weeks 6–8 postpartum): Foundational Strength

**Pending 6-week OB clearance.** Begin loading bodyweight work, deep core, glutes, posture. Still no crunching/sit-ups, planks, or impact.

**Frequency:** 3–4 sessions/week, 25–30 min, plus walking 20–30 min most days.

### Session A — Core & Posterior Chain

1. **Connection breath** — 2 × 10
2. **Glute bridge** — 3 × 10, slow tempo, exhale up
3. **Heel slides (supine, neutral spine)** — 2 × 8/side
4. **Dead bug — arms only** — 2 × 8/side (no leg lowering yet)
5. **Bird-dog — opposite arm/leg, slow** — 3 × 6/side
6. **Clamshells** — 2 × 12/side
7. **Wall sit** — 3 × 20 sec
8. **Side-lying leg lifts** — 2 × 10/side

### Session B — Standing Strength & Posture

1. **Connection breath standing** — 2 × 10
2. **Bodyweight squat to mat (sit-to-stand if needed)** — 3 × 10
3. **Split stance, static hold with breath** — 2 × 20 sec/side
4. **Wall push-up** — 3 × 8–10
5. **Standing hip hinge (no load)** — 3 × 10
6. **Standing band/towel row (towel anchored or isometric pulls)** — 3 × 10
7. **Calf raises** — 2 × 15
8. **Standing thoracic rotations** — 2 × 8/side

### Session C — Mobility & Pelvic Floor

1. **90/90 hip rocks** — 2 × 6/side
2. **Happy baby (gentle)** — 60 sec
3. **Pelvic floor relaxation (deep squat against wall, supported)** — 2 × 30 sec
4. **Quadruped rocking** — 2 × 8
5. **Supine figure-4 stretch** — 45 sec/side
6. **Thread the needle** — 2 × 5/side

### Scar mobilisation (once fully healed, dry, and cleared)
- Daily, 2–3 min. Pads of fingers, gentle skin glide above, below, then directly over scar. Small circles, then horizontal and vertical stretches. Should not be painful.

---

## PHASE 3 — Weeks 5–6 (Client weeks 8–10 postpartum): Progressive Loading

**Goal:** Build volume, introduce light dynamic core, single-leg work, push/pull patterns. Reassess diastasis. Still no impact or heavy flexion-based abs.

**Frequency:** 4 sessions/week, 30–35 min. Walking continues; can add inclines.

### Session A — Lower Body & Core

1. **Glute bridge with march** — 3 × 8/side (watch for doming — regress if present)
2. **Goblet squat to mat (hold water bottle/baby if comfortable)** — 3 × 10
3. **Reverse lunge** — 3 × 8/side
4. **Single-leg glute bridge** — 3 × 8/side
5. **Dead bug — full (opposite arm and leg)** — 3 × 6/side
6. **Side plank from knees** — 2 × 15 sec/side
7. **Bird-dog with hold** — 3 × 6/side, 2-sec pause

### Session B — Upper Body & Posture

1. **Incline push-up (against couch or low surface)** — 3 × 8
2. **Towel/band row, tall kneeling** — 3 × 12
3. **Tall kneeling overhead press (water bottles or light load)** — 3 × 10
4. **Prone Y-T-W** — 2 × 8 each
5. **Quadruped shoulder taps (slow)** — 2 × 6/side
6. **Bear hold (knees hovering 1 inch)** — 3 × 10 sec
7. **Wall slides** — 2 × 10

### Session C — Lower Body & Mobility

1. **Step-up (onto stair)** — 3 × 8/side
2. **Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on couch)** — 3 × 6/side
3. **Hip airplane / single-leg balance reach** — 2 × 6/side
4. **Glute bridge isometric hold** — 2 × 30 sec
5. **Mobility flow** — 5 min: 90/90, world's greatest stretch, cat-cow

### Session D — Active Recovery / Yoga Flow
30 min gentle flow emphasising breath, hips, thoracic mobility. Avoid deep backbends and any pose that domes the belly.

---

## PHASE 4 — Weeks 7–9 (Client weeks 10–13 postpartum): Strength & Capacity

**Goal:** Build true strength endurance, longer holds, single-leg power prep, controlled loaded core. Reassess DR — if closed/well-managed, introduce more direct anterior core. Still avoid full sit-ups and high-impact unless pelvic floor is asymptomatic.

**Frequency:** 4 sessions/week, 35–45 min.

### Session A — Lower Body Strength

1. **Tempo squat (3-sec down)** — 4 × 10
2. **Reverse lunge with reach** — 3 × 10/side
3. **Single-leg deadlift (bodyweight or light load)** — 3 × 8/side
4. **Glute bridge march** — 3 × 12/side
5. **Side plank from feet (or knees)** — 3 × 20 sec/side
6. **Dead bug with load (book in hands)** — 3 × 8/side

### Session B — Upper Body Strength

1. **Push-up — incline progressing toward floor** — 4 × 6–10
2. **Single-arm towel row, hip hinge position** — 3 × 10/side
3. **Pike push-up (toes on mat, hips high)** — 3 × 6
4. **Tall kneeling press** — 3 × 10
5. **Bear crawl forward/back (slow)** — 3 × 4 lengths
6. **Hollow hold — knees bent, hands on thighs** — 3 × 15 sec (only if no doming)

### Session C — Full Body Circuit

3 rounds, 40 sec work / 20 sec rest:
- Squat → Push-up → Reverse lunge (alternating) → Bird-dog → Glute bridge → Dead bug → Side plank

### Session D — Mobility, Yoga, Walk
Long walk 30–45 min (incline or hilly) + 20 min yoga.

### Introduce mini-impact testing late in Phase 4
- **Pelvic floor readiness test (only if asymptomatic and DR managed):** 10 heel raises → 10 jumping jacks in place → 1 min jog. Watch for leaking, heaviness, pain, doming. If any, regress and consider pelvic health referral before continuing.

---

## PHASE 5 — Weeks 10–12 (Client weeks 13–16 postpartum): Return to Function

**Goal:** Tolerate light impact (if PF test passed), progress core, return to a "normal" general-strength template she can carry forward.

**Frequency:** 4–5 sessions/week, 40–45 min.

### Session A — Lower Body + Light Plyo

1. **Squat (tempo or paused)** — 4 × 10
2. **Reverse lunge** — 3 × 10/side
3. **Single-leg deadlift** — 3 × 8/side
4. **Pogo hops (low, 2 inches)** — 3 × 20 sec — only if PF asymptomatic
5. **Lateral bounds (small)** — 3 × 6/side
6. **Side plank with reach** — 3 × 8/side

### Session B — Upper Body Strength

1. **Push-up (full or elevated as needed)** — 4 × 8
2. **Towel row** — 4 × 12
3. **Pike push-up** — 3 × 8
4. **Tall kneeling press** — 4 × 10
5. **Hollow hold** — 3 × 20 sec
6. **Dead bug with load** — 3 × 10/side

### Session C — Full Body Conditioning

EMOM 20 min, alternating:
- Min 1: 10 squats
- Min 2: 8 push-ups
- Min 3: 10 reverse lunges (total)
- Min 4: 30-sec side plank (alternate sides each round)

### Session D — Posterior Chain & Core

1. **Single-leg glute bridge** — 4 × 10/side
2. **Hip hinge** — 4 × 10
3. **Bird-dog** — 3 × 8/side
4. **Bear crawl** — 3 × 6 lengths
5. **Dead bug** — 3 × 10/side
6. **Side plank w/ hip dip** — 3 × 8/side

### Session E — Walk / Yoga / Active Recovery

---

## Recovery & Lifestyle Notes

- **Sleep:** Likely fragmented. Encourage naps and don't shame missed sessions.
- **Hydration:** Especially if breastfeeding — aim 2.5–3 L/day.
- **Nutrition (broad strokes, defer specifics to RD if she has clinical needs):** Adequate protein (1.6–2.0 g/kg), don't aggressively deficit if breastfeeding (~300–500 kcal extra needed), prioritise iron, omega-3s, vitamin D, calcium.
- **Red flags to stop & refer:** Bright red bleeding returning, pelvic heaviness/pressure, incontinence with exercise, scar pain or pulling, persistent low back/SIJ pain, doming or coning of the belly.
- **Mental health:** Postpartum anxiety/depression is common. Be a check-in point and know your referral pathway.

## Key Progression Principles

1. **Breath leads movement.** Exhale on exertion through Phase 1–3.
2. **Watch for doming** at every core progression — if it appears, regress.
3. **Pelvic floor symptoms = regress.** Don't push through leaking or heaviness.
4. **Trust the timeline, not the calendar.** If a phase needs an extra week, take it.
5. **End-state at week 12:** She should be confident bodyweight strong, walking briskly, tolerating light impact, with a reconnected core — ready to enter a general strength programme (or progress to weighted training if she has access).

Let me know if you'd like a printable client-facing version, a diastasis recti screening protocol, or a load-progression guide for when she gets access to dumbbells.

# Nutrition Plan — Breastfeeding-Supportive

**Important upfront:** As a trainer, you're operating within scope when you provide general healthy-eating guidance and macronutrient targets. Anything clinical — supplementation beyond standard postnatal, food allergies/intolerances in baby, suspected low supply, significant weight concerns, history of disordered eating — should be referred to a registered dietitian (ideally one with lactation experience) or her GP/IBCLC. Flag this to her clearly.

---

## Guiding Principles

1. **Nourish first, leanness later.** Milk supply, energy, mood, and recovery depend on adequate intake. Aggressive deficits in the first 6 months postpartum can suppress supply and tank recovery.
2. **Eat enough.** Lactation costs roughly **450–500 kcal/day** above her pre-pregnancy maintenance for an exclusively breastfeeding mother. Partial breastfeeding scales down proportionally.
3. **Protein, fluids, and micronutrients are non-negotiable.** These are the levers that matter most.
4. **Frequency over perfection.** Frequent, easy-to-grab meals beat elaborate cooking with a newborn.

---

## Calorie Target

Assuming an average active 33-year-old female (~65–70 kg), exclusively or predominantly breastfeeding:

- **Estimated maintenance (non-lactating):** ~1,900–2,100 kcal
- **Lactation add-on:** +450–500 kcal
- **Total target:** **~2,400–2,600 kcal/day**

If her primary goal is gradual fat loss while breastfeeding, a **small** deficit of ~300 kcal below this (so ~2,100–2,300 kcal) is generally considered safe after milk supply is well-established (~8–12 weeks postpartum). **Do not go below ~1,800 kcal/day while breastfeeding** without RD oversight — supply often drops.

Adjust by ±200 kcal based on hunger, energy, supply, and her body's response over 2–3 weeks.

---

## Macronutrient Targets

Based on ~70 kg bodyweight; adjust to her actual weight.

| Macro | Target | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Protein** | 1.8–2.2 g/kg → **125–155 g/day** | Tissue repair post-C-section, milk production, satiety, lean mass during training |
| **Fat** | 0.8–1.0 g/kg → **55–70 g/day** | Hormone production, vitamin absorption, milk fat composition |
| **Carbohydrate** | Fill remainder → **280–340 g/day** | Energy for training, milk lactose, mood, sleep |
| **Fibre** | 25–35 g/day | Postpartum digestion; constipation is common |
| **Fluids** | **3–3.5 L/day** | Milk is ~87% water; thirst lags need |

---

## Micronutrients That Matter Most Postpartum & Lactating

Prioritise food sources; supplement gaps.

- **Iron** — blood loss recovery. Red meat, liver (1×/wk), lentils, spinach, fortified cereals. Pair plant sources with vitamin C. *Ask GP about ferritin if she's fatigued beyond expected.*
- **Vitamin D** — most postpartum women are deficient. Continue prenatal or take **1,000–2,000 IU/day**. Baby also typically supplemented.
- **Omega-3 (DHA)** — brain development for baby, mood for mum. **200–300 mg DHA/day**. 2 portions oily fish/wk (salmon, sardines, mackerel) or algal oil supplement.
- **Calcium** — **1,000 mg/day**. Dairy, fortified plant milks, sardines with bones, tofu, leafy greens.
- **Iodine** — increased need during lactation (~290 mcg/day). Dairy, eggs, white fish, iodised salt. Most prenatals contain it.
- **Choline** — 550 mg/day. Eggs (especially yolks), liver, salmon.
- **B12** — particularly if vegetarian/vegan; supplement required if vegan.
- **Continue her prenatal multivitamin** throughout breastfeeding.

---

## Plate Template (Easy Visual)

Every meal, aim for:
- **¼ plate protein** (palm-sized portion: ~30–40 g protein)
- **¼ plate starchy carb** (cupped hand: rice, oats, potato, bread, pasta)
- **½ plate vegetables/fruit** (variety, colour)
- **Thumb of fats** (olive oil, avocado, nuts, butter)
- **Fluid** with every meal

Three meals + 2–3 snacks works better than 3 large meals for most breastfeeding mothers — energy and hunger swing hard.

---

## Sample Day (~2,500 kcal, ~140 g protein)

**On waking (often during night feed):** Large glass of water + handful of nuts or a banana. Keep these by the bed.

**Breakfast (~600 kcal):**
- 3-egg omelette with spinach, feta, tomato
- 2 slices wholegrain toast with butter
- 1 piece fruit
- Coffee (limit caffeine to ~200–300 mg/day)

**Mid-morning snack (~300 kcal):**
- Greek yogurt (200 g) + berries + 1 tbsp honey + 2 tbsp granola/oats

**Lunch (~650 kcal):**
- Chicken thigh (150 g cooked) or salmon
- 1 cup cooked rice or quinoa
- Mixed roasted veg
- Drizzle olive oil, lemon
- Side salad

**Afternoon snack (~300 kcal):**
- Wholegrain crackers + hummus + cheese, OR
- "Lactation"-style oat bites (oats, peanut butter, flax, dark chocolate)

**Dinner (~550 kcal):**
- Lean beef mince stir-fry or lentil dahl
- Wholegrain noodles or basmati rice
- Stir-fried vegetables
- Sesame oil, ginger, garlic

**Evening (optional, ~150 kcal):**
- Warm milk + cinnamon, or cottage cheese + fruit

**Across the day:** 3–3.5 L water. A glass at every feed is an easy anchor.

---

## Foods to Emphasise

- **Protein:** Eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, chicken, lean beef, salmon/sardines, tofu, lentils, whey protein (fine while breastfeeding).
- **Iron-rich:** Red meat (1–2×/wk), liver pâté, lentils, dark leafy greens, fortified cereals.
- **Calcium/iodine:** Dairy or fortified alternatives, sardines, eggs.
- **Omega-3:** Salmon, mackerel, sardines, walnuts, flax, chia.
- **Galactagogue foods (mild evidence, mostly via adequate calories/hydration):** Oats, barley, fenugreek-containing foods, fennel, brewer's yeast. Don't oversell — supply responds best to frequent feeding/pumping and adequate intake overall.
- **Complex carbs:** Oats, sweet potato, brown rice, wholegrain bread — sustained energy for night feeds.

## Foods to Limit (Not Eliminate)

- **Alcohol:** Best avoided. If consumed, 1 standard drink occasionally, timed immediately after a feed; ~2 hrs to clear per drink. No need to "pump and dump" unless drinking more.
- **Caffeine:** ≤200–300 mg/day (about 2–3 cups coffee). Some babies are sensitive.
- **High-mercury fish:** Limit shark, swordfish, marlin, king mackerel. Tuna ≤2 portions/wk.
- **Ultra-processed snacks:** Not banned, but they crowd out nutrient-dense options when she's exhausted and grabbing what's easy.

---

## Practical Strategies for a New Mum

1. **Batch cook on weekends.** Soups, stews, traybakes, overnight oats, hard-boiled eggs.
2. **Snack stations.** Keep a basket of grab-and-go food near her feeding chair: nuts, fruit, protein bars, oat bites, jerky, cheese.
3. **Water bottle at every feeding spot.** Refill every time she sits down to feed.
4. **One-handed meals.** Wraps, smoothies, overnight oats, energy balls — designed for holding a baby.
5. **Freezer meals.** If anyone offers help, ask for cooked food, not visits.
6. **Don't skip breakfast.** Setting a high-protein anchor in the morning prevents the 3pm sugar crash + cortisol spike.
7. **Protein shake as a rescue tool.** When a meal won't happen, 1 scoop whey + milk + banana + oats + peanut butter ≈ 500 kcal, 35 g protein, 2 minutes.

---

## Around-Training Nutrition

Her sessions are short (25–45 min) and low-to-moderate intensity, so nothing fancy is needed.

- **Pre-session:** Don't train fasted. A small carb + protein snack 30–60 min before (banana + yogurt, toast + peanut butter) supports energy.
- **Post-session:** Within 1–2 hours, a proper meal with 30–40 g protein and carbs. Aligns easily with regular meals.
- **Hydration:** Extra 500 ml around sessions, on top of baseline 3 L.

---

## Weight & Body Composition Expectations

Set these expectations clearly:

- Postpartum fat loss is **slow** and that's biologically appropriate while breastfeeding.
- Expect ~**0.25–0.5 kg/week** maximum if she's targeting fat loss after week 12 postpartum.
- Many women retain 2–4 kg until weaning — this is normal hormonal physiology, not a programming failure.
- **Recomposition** (building strength + slowly losing fat at maintenance) is the better lens than aggressive cutting right now.
- Belly shape will continue changing for 6–12 months as the linea alba, uterus, and tissues remodel. Train the function, not the mirror.

---

## Red Flags to Refer Out

Send to GP/RD/IBCLC if:
- Persistent supply concerns
- Significant fatigue despite adequate sleep windows
- Hair loss beyond typical postpartum shedding + brittle nails (consider iron, thyroid)
- Low mood, anxiety, intrusive thoughts — postpartum mental health screen
- Disordered relationship with food or rapid restrictive intent
- Baby showing signs of food intolerance (severe reflux, bloody stools, eczema)

---

## Simple Weekly Check-ins You Can Do as Her Trainer

Every 2 weeks ask:
1. Energy on a 1–10 scale?
2. Sleep total (rough)?
3. Hunger — manageable or relentless?
4. Mood?
5. Any drop in milk supply she's noticed?
6. Hitting ~3 L water and a protein source at every meal?

If energy or supply drop, **add 200–300 kcal/day**, mostly from carbs and fat, before changing anything else.

# Strength Progression Addendum — Loaded Training Path

This builds on the 12-week return programme and gives you a clear pathway for adding load as she progresses, plus a continuation template for weeks 13+ once she's cleared the foundational phases.

**Equipment assumption:** She'll likely acquire dumbbells (or kettlebells) and possibly a resistance band set somewhere between weeks 6–10. I'll write this so you can introduce load whenever the equipment arrives, gated by readiness rather than calendar.

---

## Readiness Gates Before Adding External Load

Don't load just because the calendar says so. She needs to demonstrate:

1. **No diastosis doming or coning** during bodyweight bird-dog, dead bug, and glute bridge march.
2. **No pelvic floor symptoms** — no leaking, heaviness, or pressure during or after bodyweight sessions.
3. **Clean bodyweight squat to mat** with neutral spine and exhale-driven control.
4. **Clean hip hinge** — bodyweight Romanian deadlift with neutral spine, no compensations.
5. **Incline push-ups for 3 × 8** with full ROM, no rib flare or belly doming.
6. **C-section scar fully healed**, mobilising well, no pulling sensation with movement.
7. **Sleep averaging ≥5 hrs/24** (fragmented is fine). Below this, regress, don't progress.

Tick all seven → load. Miss any → repeat the previous phase block with bodyweight.

---

## Load Selection Principles for a Postpartum Client

- **Start lighter than you think.** Her connective tissue is still under the influence of relaxin for ~3–6 months postpartum (longer if breastfeeding). Joints feel "loose."
- **Reps in reserve (RIR) of 3–4** through Phase 4 and most of Phase 5. No grinders. No failure.
- **Tempo over load.** A 3-sec eccentric with light weight builds more safely than a heavy fast rep.
- **Bilateral before unilateral loaded.** Goblet squat before loaded split squat.
- **Hinge with caution.** Romanian deadlifts are great but go light and slow — the posterior chain is often deconditioned and the lower back is vulnerable.
- **Breathe and brace, don't Valsalva.** Exhale on exertion through at least Phase 5. No breath-holding under load — pelvic floor pressure management is still rebuilding.
- **Progress one variable at a time:** load OR reps OR tempo OR complexity — never two at once.

---

## Where to Add Load Within the Existing 12-Week Plan

### Phase 2 (Programme weeks 3–4) — No external load
Bodyweight only. Add a household object (water bottle, small backpack) only for grip familiarity, not load.

### Phase 3 (Programme weeks 5–6) — Optional light load if gates met

If she has dumbbells and meets the readiness gates, introduce light load on these movements only:

- **Goblet squat to mat:** 5–8 kg DB or KB → 3 × 10
- **Single-arm row, hip hinge:** 5–7 kg DB → 3 × 10/side
- **Tall kneeling overhead press:** 3–5 kg DBs → 3 × 10
- **Glute bridge with DB on hips:** 8–10 kg → 3 × 10
- **Reverse lunge:** keep bodyweight this phase

Everything else stays bodyweight.

### Phase 4 (Programme weeks 7–9) — Light–moderate load

Working sets, RIR 3–4:

| Movement | Starting Load | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 8–12 kg | 4 × 8–10 |
| Romanian deadlift (DBs) | 2 × 5–8 kg | 3 × 10 |
| Reverse lunge | 2 × 4–6 kg DBs | 3 × 8/side |
| Single-arm row | 7–10 kg | 3 × 10/side |
| Floor press (DB) | 2 × 5–8 kg | 3 × 10 |
| Tall kneeling press | 2 × 4–6 kg | 3 × 10 |
| Single-leg DL (light) | 1 × 5–8 kg | 3 × 8/side |
| Suitcase carry | 1 × 8–12 kg | 3 × 20 m |

### Phase 5 (Programme weeks 10–12) — Building genuine strength

| Movement | Load Target | Sets × Reps |
|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 12–16 kg | 4 × 8 |
| Romanian deadlift | 2 × 8–12 kg | 4 × 8 |
| Bulgarian split squat | 2 × 5–8 kg | 3 × 8/side |

## Weeks 13–20 — Continuation Strength Block

Once she finishes the 12-week return programme, run this 8-week block to consolidate strength and transition her toward general training.

**Structure:** 3 strength sessions/week + 1–2 walks/yoga sessions. ~45 min per session.

### Session A — Lower Body Strength Focus

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |

| Goblet squat | 4 × 8 | Add 1–2 kg when all sets clean at RIR 3 |
| Romanian deadlift | 4 × 8 | Light, hinge focus |

### Session B — Upper Body & Core

| Floor press | 4 × 8 | DBs; pause at chest |

| Farmer's carry | 3 × 40 m | Heavy as form allows |
| Bear crawl | 3 × 6 lengths | |

**KB swing caveat:** Only introduce once she's nailed RDL form, has no pelvic floor symptoms, and can exhale-brace through impact. If any leaking or heaviness — pull it immediately.

---

## Progression Method — How to Add Load Each Week

Use **double progression** — simple and forgiving:

1. **Set a rep range** (e.g., 8–10 reps for 4 sets).
2. Hit the **top of the range on all sets** with RIR 3 → next session, add **1–2 kg** and drop back to the bottom of the range.
3. Repeat.

Example for goblet squat 4 × 8–10:
- Week 1: 10 kg × 4 × 8
- Week 2: 10 kg × 4 × 9
- Week 3: 10 kg × 4 × 10 ✓ → bump to 12 kg next session
- Week 4: 12 kg × 4 × 8
- And so on.

**Deload week every 4–6 weeks**, especially while still breastfeeding: drop sets to 60% load for one week. Postpartum recovery is non-linear; pre-emptive deloads prevent setbacks.

---

## Adjustments Based on Her Reality

### If she's not sleeping (under 4 hrs total)
- Drop one set off every exercise.
- Hold loads where they are; don't progress this week.
- Replace one strength session with a walk + mobility.

### If she's leaking, doming, or feels pelvic heaviness
- **Stop loaded core and impact immediately.**
- Regress to Phase 3 core work for 1–2 weeks.
- Refer to a pelvic health physio.
- Lower body strength can continue but reduce load by 30% and avoid Valsalva.

### If she returns to her menstrual cycle
- Energy and strength will fluctuate. Programme heavier work in follicular phase (post-period to ovulation), lighter in late luteal if she's symptomatic.
- This is more nuanced if she's still breastfeeding — cycle can be erratic.

### If she's losing weight too fast (>0.5 kg/week sustained)
- Bump calories per the nutrition plan **before** reducing training load.
- Under-fuelling will tank strength progress and supply.

---

## Long-Term View (Months 6–12 Postpartum)

By 6 months postpartum she should be capable of:
- Goblet squat with 16–20 kg for sets of 8
- Romanian deadlift with 2 × 12–15 kg DBs for sets of 8
- Full push-ups for sets of 5–8
- Bent-over row with 2 × 10–12 kg
- Farmer's carry with 2 × 14–16 kg

By 9–12 months postpartum, if she has access to a barbell or heavier loads, she can transition to a standard 3-day full-body strength template (e.g., squat/bench/row pattern with linear progression). At that point, treat her as a generally trained client, with two caveats that persist until she's done breastfeeding:

1. Continue prioritising exhale-on-exertion and avoid maximal Valsalva.
2. Keep a pelvic floor check-in in your bi-weekly questions.

---

## Quick-Reference Decision Tree for You

**Before each session, ask:**
- Sleep last night? <4 hrs → regression session.
- Any leaking, heaviness, doming since last session? → don't progress; investigate.
- Energy 1–10? <5 → hold loads, reduce volume by 1 set.
- Hit prescribed reps at RIR 3+ last session? → progress per double progression.
- Feeling strong? → still cap at RIR 2. No grinders for the first year postpartum.

# Core Training Roadmap — Getting Her Core Back Safely

Great goal, and a really common one. Here's the honest answer up front: **she's already been training her core since week 1** — just not the kind she's picturing. The breath work, dead bugs, bird-dogs, side planks, and carries in her programme are core training. They're rebuilding the deep system (transverse abdominis, pelvic floor, diaphragm, multifidus) that has to come back online *before* the superficial system (rectus abdominis, obliques) can work properly.

If you start crunching her too early, you don't get a flat stomach — you get a domed belly, a wider diastasis, and potentially a pelvic floor that fails under load. The path to the core she wants runs *through* the deep work, not around it.

Here's how to talk to her about it and how to programme it.

---

## What She Actually Needs to Understand

Sit her down and explain three things:

1. **Her abs aren't gone — they're stretched and disorganised.** The rectus abdominis was pulled 50%+ longer during pregnancy. The linea alba (the connective tissue down the middle) is still remodelling and won't be fully recovered for 6–12 months. Crunching a stretched, weak muscle just reinforces dysfunction.

2. **Diastasis recti is normal and usually self-resolves with the *right* training.** ~60% of women still have a measurable gap at 6 weeks postpartum, ~30% at 12 months. The goal isn't just closing the gap — it's building **tension** across the linea alba so the core functions as a unit. Some women have a small persistent gap forever and have rock-solid cores. Others close the gap completely but the tissue is still soft and weak.

3. **Visible abs are a body fat issue, not a training issue.** No amount of ab work will reveal a defined midsection until body fat is low enough. Right now she's breastfeeding and shouldn't be in an aggressive deficit. The plan is: rebuild function now, lose fat gradually post-weaning, *then* the core she wants is visible.

---

## The Core Training Hierarchy (Master This Sequence)

Each level must be mastered before adding the next. Most postpartum clients move through one level every 2–4 weeks, but it's individual.

### Level 1 — Reconnection (Programme weeks 1–2)
**What:** Breath-driven activation. She's already doing this.
- Diaphragmatic breathing
- Connection breath (exhale + pelvic floor lift + TVA draw)
- Pelvic tilts
- Glute bridges (yes, these are core)

**Mastery test:** Can she perform a full connection breath and feel a gentle lift of the pelvic floor + lower belly drawing in on the exhale, with full release on the inhale, lying down and standing? Yes → Level 2.

### Level 2 — Anti-Extension & Anti-Rotation, Bodyweight (Programme weeks 3–6)
**What:** Teaching the core to *resist* movement, not create it. This is the bedrock of a strong functional core.

- Dead bug (arms only → full)
- Bird-dog
- Glute bridge march
- Side plank from knees
- Wall plank → incline plank

**Mastery test:** Can she perform full dead bug 3 × 8/side and side plank from knees 3 × 20 sec/side with **no doming, no breath-holding, no rib flare, and a controlled exhale on effort**? Yes → Level 3.

### Level 3 — Loaded Anti-Movement (Programme weeks 7–9)
**What:** Adding load to the same anti-movement patterns. This is where strength really builds.

- Dead bug with load (DB or book in opposite hand)
- Bird-dog with light load on hand
- Side plank from feet
- Bear hold (knees hovering)
- Suitcase carry (huge anti-lateral-flexion stimulus)
- Pallof press (band anti-rotation)
- Half-kneeling chops/lifts

**Mastery test:** Can she carry a 12 kg suitcase 30 m without lateral lean, hold a full side plank for 30 sec/side, and perform loaded dead bugs with control? Yes → Level 4.

### Level 4 — Dynamic Core (Programme weeks 10–12)
**What:** Adding controlled movement under load and beginning to challenge the anterior core dynamically.

- Hollow hold (knees bent → tucked → extended)
- Hollow rocks (only after static hold is solid)
- Renegade row
- KB/DB windmill (light)
- Bear crawl
- Plank to push-up
- Med ball/DB chops with rotation

**Mastery test:** Hollow hold 30 sec, full side plank with hip dip, full plank 45 sec — all with no doming. Yes → Level 5.

### Level 5 — Flexion & Rotation (Weeks 13+, gated by diastasis status)
**What:** Now — and only now — we add the "ab work" she's been picturing. Crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, Russian twists, hanging knee raises.

**This is the gate:** Diastosis must be functional (gap ≤2 fingers AND good tension generated across the linea alba on a head-lift test). If there's still a soft, doughy gap or visible doming when she lifts her head, **stay at Level 4** and refer to a pelvic health physio.

---

## How to Test Her Diastasis (Do This Now and Every 2–3 Weeks)

You may have already done this, but in case not:

1. Client lies supine, knees bent, feet flat.
2. Place 2 fingers horizontally just above her navel.
3. Ask her to slowly lift her head and shoulders off the mat (small crunch).
4. Feel:
   - **Width** of the gap (1 finger, 2, 3+?)
   - **Depth** — do your fingers sink in, or does the tissue push back?
   - **Doming** — does the midline bulge up?
5. Repeat above and below the navel.

**Interpret:**
- **≤2 finger width + firm tension + no doming:** Functional. Level 4 work fine. Can test-introduce Level 5 cautiously.
- **2–3 fingers + some tension:** Stay at Level 3–4. Avoid crunches/sit-ups/planks-from-feet.
- **3+ fingers, soft, deep, doming:** Refer to pelvic health physio. Stay at Levels 1–2.

---

## When Can She Add "Real" Ab Work?

**Honest timeline for most uncomplicated C-section clients:**

- **Crunches, sit-ups, V-ups:** Earliest at **Programme Week 10–12** if diastasis is fully functional. More commonly **Week 13–16** (months 4–5 postpartum). Some women safely wait 6 months. **No rush.**
- **Hanging leg raises, toes-to-bar, ab-wheel rollouts:** **6+ months postpartum minimum**, and only if she's nailed all Level 4 progressions and has zero symptoms.
- **Heavy weighted crunches/decline sit-ups:** Honestly, ever? They're not necessary and the risk-reward for postpartum is poor. Cable Pallof presses, loaded carries, and hanging knee raises build a far better-looking and stronger core than weighted crunches.

---

## Updated Core Programming Across Her 12 Weeks

Slot this into her existing sessions:

### Programme Weeks 1–2 (Phase 1)
- Connection breath: daily, 2 × 10
- Pelvic tilts: daily, 2 × 10

### Programme Weeks 3–4 (Phase 2)
**3 core sessions/week, integrated into her existing sessions:**
- Dead bug (arms only): 2 × 8/side
- Bird-dog: 3 × 6/side
- Glute bridge: 3 × 10
- Side-lying leg lifts: 2 × 10/side

### Programme Weeks 5–6 (Phase 3)
- Dead bug (full): 3 × 6/side
- Bird-dog with hold: 3 × 6/side
- Glute bridge march: 3 × 8/side
- Side plank from knees: 2 × 15 sec/side
- Bear hold: 2 × 10 sec

### Programme Weeks 7–9 (Phase 4) — Load enters
- Dead bug with light DB: 3 × 8/side
- Side plank from feet: 3 × 20 sec/side

- Pallof press (band): 3 × 10/side

### Programme Weeks 10–12 (Phase 5) — Dynamic core

- **Re-test diastasis at week 12.** If functional, cautiously test-introduce a single set of slow crunches and assess.

- Reverse crunch: 2 × 10

**Watch for:** doming during any rep → cut the set, regress. Leaking or pelvic heaviness → stop, refer.

---

## What She Should Avoid Right Now (and Why)

| Movement | Avoid Until | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Crunches, sit-ups | Diastasis functional + ~Week 12+ | Increase intra-abdominal pressure on a stretched linea alba; reinforce doming |
| Russian twists | Month 4+ | Rotation under flexion is the worst combination for linea alba |
| V-ups, jackknives | Month 5+ | Maximum flexion + leverage = guaranteed doming |
| Ab wheel rollouts | 6+ months minimum | Extreme anti-extension demand; pelvic floor and linea alba both vulnerable |
| Hanging leg raises | 6+ months | Heavy demand; needs full deep core integration first |
| Toes-to-bar | When she's fully reconditioned, often 9–12 months | Same as above + grip/shoulder demands |
| Heavy Valsalva lifting | Throughout breastfeeding | Pelvic floor pressure management still rebuilding |

---

## What to Tell Her This Week

A direct script you can use:

> "I hear you on wanting your core back, and we're going to get there — but I need you to trust the process. The work we've been doing *is* core training; it's just rebuilding the foundation that your abs have to anchor onto. If we skip ahead to crunches now, your belly will actually push out *more*, not flatten. Around week 10–12 we'll test where your abs are, and if they're ready, we'll start adding the work you're picturing. In the meantime, you're going to feel your midsection getting noticeably stronger, tighter, and more controlled from the work we're already doing — most women say their belly looks flatter from the deep work alone, before we ever add a single crunch."

Then show her the diastasis test. Test her now. Re-test every 2–3 weeks so she can **see** progress. That visible improvement is what keeps her bought in.

---

## Final Reality Check

The clients who get the best long-term cores postpartum are the ones who are patient in months 1–6 and consistent in months 6–18. The ones who rush to crunches in month 2 are still complaining about a "mum tummy" two years later. The deep work is the shortcut, even though it doesn't feel like one.

# Phase 3 Intensified — Building a Client Who Feels Strong by Week 12

Good instinct, and a reasonable ask **if** she's hitting her readiness gates. Phase 3 (programme weeks 5–6, ~8–10 weeks postpartum) is actually the right place to push — she's past the 6-week clearance, the deep core foundation is laid, and she has time to consolidate gains before week 12. But "push intensity" postpartum doesn't mean what it means for a general client. Let me show you what it does mean.

---

## What "Intensity" Means Here

For a postpartum client at 8–10 weeks, you have four intensity levers. Use them in this order:

1. **Tempo** (slower eccentrics, pauses) — safest, highest return on investment right now
2. **Volume** (more sets, more reps) — second safest, drives hypertrophy and work capacity
3. **Density** (less rest, supersets, circuits) — moderate risk; watch pelvic floor under fatigue
4. **Load** (heavier weight) — useful, but ceilinged by RIR 3 and her connective tissue status

You'll pull all four levers in this revised Phase 3, but tempo and volume do most of the work. Load comes up modestly. Density gets introduced carefully at the end of the phase.

---

## Non-Negotiable Gates Before You Push

Before intensifying Phase 3, confirm:

- **Diastasis** functional (gap ≤2 fingers + tension, no doming on bird-dog/dead bug).
- **Zero pelvic floor symptoms** in current training — no leaking, no heaviness, no pressure.
- **Sleep averaging ≥5 hrs/24** (fragmented is fine).
- **C-section scar** mobilising well, no pulling.
- **She's recovering between sessions** — soreness gone in 48 hrs, energy stable.

If any of these is shaky, **don't intensify** — repeat baseline Phase 3 instead. The week-12 goal isn't worth a setback that costs her a month.

---

**Tempo notation:** eccentric–pause–concentric–pause. So 3-1-1-0 = 3 sec down, 1 sec pause, 1 sec up, no pause at top.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Romanian deadlift (DBs) | 4 × 10 | 3-1-1-0 | 2 × 5–8 kg | 75 sec |
| Single-leg deadlift | 3 × 8/side | 3-0-1-0 | 1 × 5–8 kg | 60 sec |
| Step-up onto stair | 3 × 8/side | 2-0-1-0 | BW or 2 × 4–6 kg | 60 sec |
| Glute bridge with march | 3 × 10/side | 2-0-2-0 | BW or DB on hips | 45 sec |
| Bird-dog with hold | 3 × 8/side | 2-3-2-0 | 3-sec hold at extension | 45 sec |
| Suitcase carry | 3 × 30 m | — | 1 × 8–12 kg | 60 sec |

### Session D — Upper Body & Core Density

Run as a **circuit**, 3 rounds, 45 sec work / 15 sec transition, 90 sec rest between rounds:

1. Push-up (any progression)
2. Single-arm row (left)
3. Single-arm row (right)
4. Tall kneeling press
5. Dead bug
6. Side plank (alternate sides each round)

This is her introduction to density work. Watch breath quality — if she's holding her breath or leaking, **kill the circuit and revert to straight sets**.

### Session E — Conditioning + Mobility

- 25–35 min brisk walk with inclines if available
- 15 min mobility flow: 90/90 hip work, thoracic openers, hip flexor stretch, deep squat hold

---

## Week-by-Week Progression Within Phase 3

### Programme Week 5

- Establish loads at **RIR 4** (could do 4 more reps).
- Hit the tempos precisely. Tempo is the lever, not load.
- All circuit work as **straight sets** this week — defer Session D's circuit format until Week 6.
- End-of-week diastasis check.

### Programme Week 6

- Reassess loads — if Week 5 felt easy, add 1–2 kg on compound lifts.
- Now at **RIR 3**.
- Introduce circuit format in Session D.
- Add one set to two key lifts (goblet squat and RDL go to 5 × 8–10).
- End-of-week diastasis check + symptom check.

---

## Where the "Feel Strong" Effect Comes From

She'll feel dramatically stronger by week 12 not because of the load on the bar, but because of:

1. **Tempo work building tendon stiffness and motor control** — she'll move with more authority through every range.
2. **Volume driving hypertrophy** — visible muscle tone returns in the glutes, back, and shoulders within 4–6 weeks of sufficient volume.
3. **Loaded carries** — possibly the highest-ROI "feel strong" exercise in postpartum training. Add suitcase carries, farmer's carries, and bear hugs liberally.
4. **Single-leg work** — exposes and corrects asymmetries, builds glute strength fast, and translates instantly to feeling powerful in daily life (stairs, getting off the floor with baby).
5. **Removing the deep-core "training wheels"** — by mid-Phase 3 she should feel her core *holding* her under load rather than her thinking about it. That feeling is what she's actually after when she says "I want to feel strong."

---

## What You're NOT Doing to "Push Intensity"

To be explicit, "intensifying" Phase 3 does **not** mean:

- ❌ Training to failure
- ❌ Heavy 1–5 rep loading
- ❌ HIIT, burpees, jump squats, box jumps (no impact yet)
- ❌ Crunch-based ab work
- ❌ Maximal-effort grinders
- ❌ Long high-intensity conditioning sessions
- ❌ Two-a-days
- ❌ Skipping the warm-up or mobility

These are the things that feel intense in the moment but cost her recovery and risk her pelvic floor and linea alba. The intensification above produces a much stronger client at week 12 with no setbacks.

---

## How to Talk to Her About This

She wants to feel strong. Validate that, and reframe what strong looks like for her right now:

> "We're going to push hard the next two weeks — but the kind of hard that builds you, not breaks you. You'll be lifting more, doing more work, and you'll feel it. What you won't feel is wrecked. If at any point in the next two weeks you're leaking, doming, or feeling pelvic pressure, that's not 'push through it' — that's a signal we go back a step. Tell me immediately. Everything else, we attack."

---

## Adjusting Phase 4 to Match

Because you've raised the floor in Phase 3, you can raise the ceiling in Phase 4. Concretely:

- Goblet squat target by week 9: **14–16 kg for 4 × 8**
- RDL target by week 9: **2 × 10–12 kg for 4 × 8**
- Push-up: most clients hit **full push-ups for 3 × 6** by week 9 with this Phase 3
- Suitcase carry: **14–16 kg for 30 m**
- Side plank: full from feet, 30 sec/side

Phase 5 then becomes about **expressing** that strength rather than building it from scratch — you can introduce light KB swings (if she has one), pogo hops (PF-test gated), and the first single-set test of a slow tempo crunch if her diastasis screens clean.

---

## Week 12 "Feel Strong" Benchmarks

If she nails the intensified Phase 3 and the rest of the programme runs clean, she should hit these by week 12 (and be able to feel them):

- Full bodyweight push-up × 5–8
- Goblet squat 16 kg × 8 with clean tempo
- RDL 2 × 10 kg × 10
- Single-leg deadlift 10 kg × 8/side
- Side plank from feet, 30 sec/side
- Farmer's carry 2 × 12 kg × 30 m
- Bulgarian split squat with light DBs × 8/side
- Brisk 45-min walk with inclines, fully recovered next day

Show her this list now. Having concrete targets to chase is itself a strength booster — most postpartum clients have nothing tangible to aim at, and that's part of why "I want to feel strong" feels so vague to them.

---

## Red Flags That Mean Back Off Immediately

During intensified Phase 3, **regress instantly** if you see:

- Any leaking, even drops, during or after a session
- Pelvic heaviness, dragging, or pressure sensation
- Doming/coning of the belly on any rep
- Scar pulling or sharp pain
- Bleeding returning to bright red
- Sleep crashing below 4 hrs total
- Mood crashing — postpartum mental health can shift fast with overtraining

These aren't reasons to be timid — they're reasons to be precise. With clear gates, you can push harder than most postpartum programmes ever do, and produce a genuinely strong week-12 client.

# Cardio Programming — Postpartum Return

Solid addition. Cardio is genuinely important here — for cardiovascular reconditioning (pregnancy detrains the heart significantly), mental health (huge for postpartum mood regulation), fat loss readiness for post-weaning, and just feeling capable again. But postpartum cardio has two specific landmines: **pelvic floor under impact** and **energy availability while breastfeeding**. Programme it wrong and you'll either trigger leaking or tank her milk supply. Programme it right and it accelerates everything else.

---

## Guiding Principles

1. **Low-impact before impact.** Pelvic floor must demonstrably tolerate force before running, jumping, or HIIT.
2. **Zone 2 is the foundation.** Most of her cardio should be conversational pace. It builds the aerobic base without competing with strength recovery or burning through her energy budget.
3. **Cardio supplements strength, doesn't replace it.** Strength is the priority adaptation through week 12. Cardio fills around it.
4. **Fuel the work.** Add ~150–250 kcal on higher cardio days. Breastfeeding + training + under-eating = supply crash, fatigue crash, mood crash.
5. **Walking counts.** Brisk walking is genuinely effective Zone 2 cardio for a detrained postpartum client. Don't underrate it.

---

## The Heart Rate Zones (Use Effort Cues, Not Just Numbers)

She likely won't wear a chest strap. Teach her by feel:

| Zone | Effort | Talk Test | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Z1 — Recovery** | 50–60% MHR | Easy conversation, could sing | Walks, active recovery |
| **Z2 — Aerobic base** | 60–70% MHR | Can talk in full sentences, slightly breathy | Bulk of cardio work |
| **Z3 — Tempo** | 70–80% MHR | Short sentences only | Sparingly, late in programme |
| **Z4 — Threshold** | 80–90% MHR | A few words at a time | Avoid until late Phase 5 |
| **Z5 — Max** | 90%+ MHR | No talking | Avoid throughout this programme |

**Rough MHR estimate:** 220 − 33 = 187 bpm. So Z2 ≈ 112–131 bpm. Confirm with effort cues, not the number.

---

## Cardio Modalities Available at Home (Yoga Mat Only)

Without equipment, her options are:

- **Walking** (outdoors, with or without baby in carrier/pram)
- **Stair climbing** (if she has stairs)
- **Marching in place**
- **Step-ups onto a stair**
- **Shadow boxing** (later)
- **Low-impact "cardio" circuits** (squat-to-stand, reverse lunges, step-ups, marching, etc.)
- **Eventually:** jogging, then intervals (gated by pelvic floor readiness)

If she ever has access to a bike, rower, or treadmill, those are gold — fold them in immediately.

---

## Phase-by-Phase Cardio Programming

### Phase 1 (Programme Weeks 1–2) — Walking Only

She's already doing this. To formalise:

- **Frequency:** Daily
- **Duration:** 10–25 min, can split into two walks
- **Intensity:** Z1, easy pace, flat terrain
- **Goal:** Tolerance, mood, light circulation, gentle pelvic floor loading

**Watch for:** increased bleeding or red return → reduce volume. Pelvic heaviness after walks → shorten walks and add more rest.

### Phase 2 (Programme Weeks 3–4) — Walking Built Out

- **Frequency:** 5–6 days/week
- **Duration:** 20–30 min
- **Intensity:** Mostly Z1, can push to low Z2 (brisker pace) for short stretches
- **Terrain:** Introduce gentle inclines
- **Optional addition:** 1 × short low-impact circuit at end of strength session (5 min — see below)

**Low-impact mini circuit** (use once or twice/week, end of a strength session):
3 rounds, 30 sec on / 30 sec off:
- Marching in place with arm drive
- Step-ups onto stair (or step-touch if no stair)
- Squat to stand (slow)
- Standing knee drives (slow, controlled)

### Phase 3 (Programme Weeks 5–6) — Structured Cardio Begins

This is where cardio becomes its own programmed element rather than just walking.

**Weekly cardio structure:**

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Z2 walk | 30–40 min |
| Tue | Strength A + 5-min low-impact finisher | — |
| Wed | Z2 walk + hills | 30–40 min |
| Thu | Strength B | — |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk | 20–30 min |
| Sat | Strength C + low-impact cardio circuit (10 min) | — |
| Sun | Z2 walk, longer | 45–60 min |

**Total cardio:** ~3–4 hours/week, almost all Z1–Z2.

**Z2 walk progression:** Use inclines, pace, and pram weight (pushing a loaded pram up a hill is excellent low-impact cardio). She should be sweating lightly and breathing through her nose where possible.

**Low-impact cardio circuit (10 min):**
4 rounds, 40 sec on / 20 sec off:
- Step-ups (alternating)
- Reverse lunges (alternating)
- Squat to stand
- Standing march with knee drive

Heart rate should be Z2, maybe brushing low Z3 on the last round. **No breath-holding, no doming, no leaking.**

### Phase 4 (Programme Weeks 7–9) — Add Volume and Light Intensity

**Pelvic floor readiness re-test before introducing any impact** (the test from your existing programme: 10 heel raises → 10 jumping jacks → 1 min jog in place, watching for leaking, heaviness, doming).

If she passes:

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | Z2 walk or **walk-jog intervals** | 30–40 min |
| Tue | Strength A | — |
| Wed | Z2 walk with hills | 40 min |
| Thu | Strength B + low-impact conditioning circuit (12 min) | — |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk | 30 min |
| Sat | Strength C | — |
| Sun | Long Z2 walk | 60 min |

**Walk-jog intervals (if cleared):**
- 5 min Z1 walk warm-up
- 8 rounds: 1 min easy jog / 2 min walk
- 5 min Z1 walk cool-down
- Total: ~35 min

If she **fails** the PF test: stay with brisk walking + low-impact circuits. No jogging. Refer to pelvic health physio.

**Low-impact conditioning circuit (12 min):**
4 rounds, 45 sec on / 15 sec off:
- Step-ups, alternating
- Reverse lunges
- Squat to stand
- Plank shoulder taps (slow)
- Bear-position knee taps
Now in Z2–Z3 territory.

### Phase 5 (Programme Weeks 10–12) — Build Capacity

If walk-jog has been clean for 2+ weeks, progress to continuous jogging and add a small dose of higher-intensity work.

| Day | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|
| Mon | **Continuous easy jog OR Z2 walk-jog** | 25–35 min |
| Tue | Strength A | — |
| Wed | Z2 walk with hills | 45 min |
| Thu | Strength B + **intervals (light)** | — |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk | 30 min |
| Sat | Strength C | — |
| Sun | Long Z2 walk or jog/walk mix | 60–75 min |

**Light intervals (Thursday, end of session):**
- 5 min easy warm-up
- 6 rounds: 30 sec moderate effort (Z3) / 90 sec easy
- 5 min cool-down

Moderate effort = brisk jog, high step-ups, or pace-walking with arm drive. Not all-out. RPE 7/10 maximum.

**Continuous jog progression:**
- Week 10: 20 min total — 5 min walk, 10 min jog, 5 min walk
- Week 11: 25 min total — 5 min walk, 15 min jog, 5 min walk
- Week 12: 30 min total — 5 min walk, 20 min jog, 5 min walk

If she's still uncomfortable with continuous jogging at week 12, that's fine — extended walk-jog intervals are equally effective for the cardiovascular goal.

---

## Cardio Volume Targets

Across the 12 weeks she should progress to roughly:

| Phase | Total cardio/week |
|---|---|
| Phase 1 | 1.5–2.5 hrs (all walking) |
| Phase 2 | 2–3 hrs (mostly walking) |
| Phase 3 | 3–4 hrs |
| Phase 4 | 3.5–4.5 hrs |
| Phase 5 | 3.5–5 hrs |

This is well within what a recovering postpartum body can absorb without compromising strength gains or supply, *provided she's fuelling adequately*.

---

## Running Return Protocol (Once Cleared)

If running is a goal for her, the conservative postpartum return-to-running protocol looks like:

**Pre-requisites** (all must be met):
- Past 12 weeks postpartum
- Diastasis functional
- Zero pelvic floor symptoms during current training
- Passes impact readiness test (see Phase 4)
- Can single-leg squat to ~45° with control
- Can single-leg bridge × 20
- Can hop in place on one leg × 10 with no leaking, no pain
- Can run in place for 1 min with no symptoms

**Progression (assuming all met):**
- Week 1: 4 × (1 min jog / 2 min walk) × 3 sessions
- Week 2: 5 × (2 min jog / 1 min walk)
- Week 3: 4 × (3 min jog / 1 min walk)
- Week 4: 3 × (5 min jog / 2 min walk)
- Week 5: 15 min continuous jog
- Week 6: 20 min continuous jog
- Then build distance 10% per week

**Stop immediately if:** any leaking, heaviness, scar pulling, low back pain, or pelvic pain. These are pelvic floor or core insufficiency signals — refer out.

---

## Stroller / Pram Cardio (Underrated)

A loaded pram on inclines is one of the best Zone 2 tools she has. It's also realistic — she can train *with* the baby instead of finding childcare.

**Pram walking guidelines:**
- Posture: tall, ribs over hips, don't lean into the handle
- Adjust handle height so wrists are neutral
- Push with whole body, not arms
- Inclines provide automatic intensity

Once cleared to jog, **avoid running with the pram for the first 4 weeks of running**. The biomechanics of one-arm pram pushing while running are awful for a postpartum core. Build solo running first, then introduce pram running carefully.

---

## Fuelling the Cardio Days

Refer back to her nutrition plan and adjust on higher-cardio days:

- **Add ~20–40 g carbs pre-session** (banana, toast, oats) on any session over 30 min
- **Replace fluids:** add 500–750 ml water on cardio days
- **Post-session protein + carb** within 1–2 hrs (this aligns with normal meals if timed well)
- **If she does a 60+ min session, add a 200–300 kcal snack** that day — don't let the day's total drop below her target

**Watch for supply signal:** if milk supply drops noticeably within 2–3 days of increasing cardio volume, the problem is almost always under-fuelling, not the exercise itself. Add 200–300 kcal/day before pulling back the training.

---

## Cardio + Strength Day Order

When both are programmed in the same day (rare in this plan but happens with finishers):

- **Strength first, cardio second.** Always.
- If she's doing a long Z2 walk, do it on a non-strength day or several hours apart from the strength session.
- Never do high-intensity cardio (intervals) before a strength session.

---

## Watching for Overdoing It

Postpartum overtraining looks different from general-population overtraining. Watch for:

- Milk supply dipping
- Sleep getting worse despite tiredness
- Mood crash (postpartum mental health is sensitive to overtraining)
- Resting HR rising >5 bpm on morning check
- Hair shedding spike
- Recurrent illness (immune suppression)
- Cycle changes (if returned)
- Bleeding returning

Any two of these → reduce cardio volume by 30% for a week and reassess.

---

## Week 12 Cardio Benchmarks

By the end of the programme, she should comfortably hit:

- 60-min Z2 walk with hills, fully recovered next day
- 20–30 min continuous easy jog (if running is a goal and PF cleared)
- A 12-min low-impact conditioning circuit at Z2–Z3
- Light intervals (6 × 30 sec) without symptoms
- Recovery HR back to baseline within 2 min of stopping

If she hits these, she's transitioned from "postpartum" cardiovascular fitness to "trained adult" cardiovascular fitness — which is exactly the bridge week 12 is meant to cross.

---

## Quick Decision Rules for You

- Sleep <4 hrs total last night → swap any planned cardio for Z1 walk only
- Strength session today → cap cardio at Z1 walk
- Any pelvic symptoms this week → no impact, no intervals
- Milk supply dipping → add calories, hold cardio volume
- Feeling strong and recovering well → progress per plan

# HIIT for Postpartum — When and How

Honest answer: **most postpartum clients shouldn't do true HIIT in the first 6 months**, and many shouldn't in the first 9–12. HIIT is the single most overprescribed modality in postpartum training, and it's responsible for a huge proportion of pelvic floor setbacks, supply crashes, and "I worked so hard and got nowhere" stories.

That said, there's a version of high-intensity work that fits in week 10–12 of her programme, and a version of real HIIT she can earn by month 6–9. Let me break down the actual timeline and the reasoning.

---

## Why HIIT Is Higher Risk Postpartum

HIIT specifically stacks the four things her body is least ready for, all at once:

1. **Maximal intra-abdominal pressure** — blasts a still-remodelling linea alba and a recovering pelvic floor.
2. **Repeated impact under fatigue** — pelvic floor fails *more* as fatigue accumulates. Most leaking happens at minute 12, not minute 2.
3. **High cortisol + sympathetic load** — competes directly with milk supply, sleep recovery, and mood regulation.
4. **High energy cost in a short time** — easy to under-fuel, especially when she's already in a lactation deficit.

A 25-minute HIIT session can undo a week of careful rebuilding. This isn't theoretical — it's the single most common reason postpartum clients regress.

Also worth saying clearly: **HIIT is not necessary** for any of her goals. Strength + Zone 2 + walking will get her a strong, lean, capable body postpartum. HIIT is a "nice to have" that gets prioritised by clients because it feels productive, not because it produces outcomes she can't get safely elsewhere.

---

## What "HIIT" Actually Means (and What People Usually Mean)

The confusion here is real. When she says "HIIT," she probably means one of these:

| What people call HIIT | What it actually is | Postpartum readiness |
|---|---|---|
| "Tabata abs" / Insta workouts | Mostly metabolic circuits with junk exercises | Avoid the format entirely; bad even for general pop |
| 30-min "HIIT class" | Moderate-intensity circuit training | Earnable in Phase 5 as a modified version |
| Burpees, jump squats, mountain climbers | Plyometric circuit work | 6+ months postpartum minimum, gated by PF |
| Sprint intervals (running, bike, rower) | True HIIT — max effort 10–60 sec | 6–9+ months postpartum, gated by PF + running tolerance |
| CrossFit-style WODs | Mixed-modal high intensity | 9–12+ months postpartum |

So when she asks about HIIT, your first job is to find out which of these she's picturing. The path is different for each.

---

## The Progression Ladder

You move up one rung at a time. Each rung must be tolerated symptom-free for **at least 2 weeks** before progressing.

### Rung 1 — Low-impact metabolic circuits (Phase 3–4 of her current programme)
Already in her plan. Step-ups, reverse lunges, squat to stand, marching. Z2–low Z3.

### Rung 2 — Strength-based density circuits (late Phase 4 / Phase 5)
Goblet squats, RDLs, rows, pushes, carries, programmed at 45 sec on / 15 sec off. Heart rate climbs into Z3, briefly Z4. **This is the closest thing to HIIT she should do before month 6.** It hits the cardiovascular goal without impact and without max-IAP spikes.

### Rung 3 — Low-impact intervals (Phase 5, ~week 10–12)
The intervals already in her Phase 5 cardio plan: 6 × 30 sec moderate / 90 sec easy. Z3, not Z4–Z5. This is the highest intensity she earns by week 12.

### Rung 4 — Impact intervals (month 4–6 postpartum)
After she's running comfortably and has passed every PF gate cleanly for multiple weeks. Examples: jog/sprint intervals on flat ground, low pogo hops, step-up intervals. Z3–Z4. Short work bouts (15–30 sec), generous rest (90–120 sec).

### Rung 5 — Plyometric HIIT (month 6–9+ postpartum)
Jump squats, jumping lunges, burpees, mountain climbers, box jumps. Only if every PF gate is clean under fatigue, diastasis is fully functional, and she's running symptom-free.

### Rung 6 — True HIIT (month 9–12+ postpartum)
Sprint intervals (30 sec all-out / 60 sec rest), CrossFit-style WODs, max-effort circuits. This is no different from training a regular client at this point, assuming clean recovery and no symptoms.

---

## Concrete Answer: When Can YOU Add HIIT to This Client?

**Within the 12-week programme:** No true HIIT. The highest intensity she'll see is Rung 2 (strength-based density circuits) and Rung 3 (light low-impact intervals) — both already in Phase 5. This is appropriate and sufficient.

**Weeks 13–24 (months 4–6 postpartum):** Earnable Rung 4 — impact intervals — if she passes the full gate list below.

**Month 6+:** Rung 5 plyometric work if Rung 4 has been clean for 4+ weeks.

**Month 9+:** Rung 6 true HIIT if she wants it and has earned every previous rung.

If she's still breastfeeding at month 9, the supply-and-recovery consideration still applies, but the tissue-and-pelvic-floor consideration is largely resolved by then for most women.

---

## The Gate List for Each Rung

Before adding **Rung 3 (low-impact intervals, week 10–12):**
- Passed initial PF readiness test (10 heel raises, 10 jumping jacks, 1 min jog) symptom-free
- Diastosis functional (≤2 fingers, good tension, no doming)
- No symptoms during current Phase 4 training
- Sleep ≥5 hrs total most nights
- Milk supply stable

Before adding **Rung 4 (impact intervals, month 4–6):**
- All of the above, sustained for 2+ weeks
- Running symptom-free for 15–20 min continuous
- Single-leg hop × 10 each side with no leaking, no pain, no instability
- Single-leg squat to 45° controlled
- Loaded carries with bodyweight-level loads symptom-free
- No symptoms after sessions, including next-morning check (delayed leaking is real)

Before adding **Rung 5 (plyometric HIIT, month 6+):**
- All of the above
- Running 30+ min comfortably
- Box jumps from low height (15 cm) × 10 symptom-free
- Loaded squat at bodyweight (e.g., goblet squat at 25 kg) for 5 reps
- Has cycled (if returning) without supply crash or symptom flare
- No regression for 4+ weeks
- **Cleared by pelvic health physio if she's seen one** — strongly recommend a single PT assessment before this rung if she hasn't had one

Before adding **Rung 6 (true HIIT, month 9+):**
- All of the above, sustained for 4+ weeks at Rung 5
- Genuinely no symptoms under fatigue across multiple modalities
- Strength gains stable, sleep adequate, supply stable (if still BF)
- She actually wants this — don't sell her HIIT she doesn't want

---

## What to Programme Instead, If She Wants "HIIT Feel" Now

This is the practical play. She wants the *feeling* of HIIT — sweat, breath, "I worked hard." Give her that legally:

### Option A — Strength Density Block (her Phase 5 Session D already does this)
Goblet squat / row / press / carry / dead bug, programmed as 45/15 for 12–16 min. Heart rate genuinely high, real conditioning effect, zero impact, no IAP spikes.

### Option B — Stair Sprints
If she has stairs, walking up stairs at a hard pace then walking down for recovery is brilliant Z3–Z4 work with controlled impact. 6 × (walk up hard / walk down easy) is a real session.

### Option C — Incline Walk Intervals
Push the pram or walk a steep hill. 6 × (90 sec hard uphill / 90 sec easy down). Heart rate spikes, no impact, no IAP issues.

### Option D — Carry-Based Conditioning
Heavy farmer's carry for 30 m / rest 30 sec, × 8 rounds. Looks unsexy, brutal conditioning effect, perfect for postpartum.

These hit the conditioning goal with **none of the postpartum risk** of true HIIT. Sell them to her on this basis: "We're going to give you the conditioning hit you're after, without the setback risk. Same sweat, no cost."

---

## When You Do Add True HIIT (Month 6–12), Programme It Like This

When she's earned it, real HIIT for a still-breastfeeding postpartum client should look like:

- **Frequency:** 1 session/week maximum at Rung 4; 1–2 at Rung 5; 2 at Rung 6
- **Duration:** 15–20 min total including warm-up/cool-down
- **Format:** Work intervals 20–40 sec, rest intervals 60–120 sec (longer rest than you'd give a general client — this protects the pelvic floor under fatigue)
- **Ratio:** Start at 1:3 work-to-rest, progress to 1:2, never go below 1:1
- **Position in week:** Not the day before strength, not the day after a poor sleep night
- **Stop criteria mid-session:** ANY leaking, heaviness, doming → session ends. No "push through one more round."

Sample Rung 5 session at month 7+:
- 5 min easy warm-up + dynamic prep
- 8 rounds: 30 sec work / 90 sec rest
  - Rotate: jump squats / mountain climbers / pogo hops / burpees (no push-up phase initially)
- 5 min cool-down
- Total: ~20 min

---

## How to Have This Conversation With Her

She's going to push back on "no HIIT for 6 months." Here's the framing:

> "You're going to do high-intensity work — I'm going to programme it for you starting in week 10. What I'm not going to give you is jump-around-on-Instagram HIIT, because that's the single fastest way to set you back 6 weeks and lose the progress we've built. The version I'm going to give you produces the same heart rate, the same sweat, the same conditioning effect — without the leaking-during-jumping-jacks future you don't want. Around month 5 or 6 we'll start adding the plyometric stuff if you still want it. By then your body will actually handle it, and you'll get the result instead of the setback."

Most clients accept this when they understand the *why*. If she still pushes, the diastasis check + PF test usually settles it — when she sees her own belly dome on a head-lift, the conversation ends.

---

## Red Flags That Mean Drop a Rung Immediately

Even once she's earned higher rungs, regress instantly if:

- Any leaking, even one drop
- Pelvic heaviness, dragging, pressure
- Doming during any movement
- Lower back pain that wasn't there before
- Scar pulling or sensitivity returning
- Milk supply dropping within 3–5 days of the session
- Sleep degrading
- Cycle disturbance (if returned)

Drop one full rung, hold for 2 weeks, retest gates, then progress again.

---

## Summary Decision Table

| Timepoint | Highest intensity allowed |
|---|---|
| Week 1–4 of programme (4–8 wk postpartum) | Z1 walking |
| Week 5–6 (Phase 3) | Low Z3 density circuits, strength-based |
| Week 7–9 (Phase 4) | Z3 density circuits, light walk-jog if PF clear |
| Week 10–12 (Phase 5) | Light intervals at Z3, low-impact only |
| Months 4–6 postpartum | Impact intervals (Rung 4) if all gates pass |
| Months 6–9 postpartum | Plyometric HIIT (Rung 5) if Rung 4 clean |
| Months 9–12+ postpartum | True HIIT (Rung 6) if Rung 5 clean |

---

# 12-Week Postpartum Return Programme — Master Summary

**Client:** 33 y/o female, 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, OB-cleared for light activity only until 6-week check. Home, yoga mat, dumbbells acquired around weeks 5–7. Breastfeeding. Goals: safe return to fitness, restore core function, feel strong by week 12.

---

## Programme at a Glance

| Phase | Programme Weeks | Postpartum Weeks | Focus | Intensity Ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1–2 | 4–6 | Restorative breath + walking | Z1 |
| 2 | 3–4 | 6–8 | Foundational bodyweight strength | Z1–low Z2 |
| 3 | 5–6 | 8–10 | Strength build, light load introduced | Z2–low Z3 |
| 4 | 7–9 | 10–13 | Progressive loading + walk-jog | Z3 |
| 5 | 10–12 | 13–16 | Strength expression, light intervals | Z3 (briefly) |

**Headline rule:** No HIIT, no crunches, no impact in the 12 weeks. She'll be genuinely strong by week 12 — that's the win.

---

## Universal Principles Across All 12 Weeks

1. Breath leads movement — exhale on exertion, no breath-holding under load.
2. Watch for doming/coning at every core progression — appears → regress.
3. Any leaking, heaviness, or pelvic pressure → stop, drop intensity, consider PF physio referral.
4. RIR 3–4 throughout — no grinders, no failure, no max effort.
5. Sleep <4 hrs total → regression session, not progression.
6. Diastasis check at end of each phase.
7. Fuel the work — under-eating crashes supply faster than overtraining does.

---

## PHASE 1 — Programme Weeks 1–2 (Postpartum Weeks 4–6)

**Focus:** Reconnection. No load, no flexion, no impact.
**Sessions:** Daily 10–15 min + walking.

### Daily Session — Breath & Reconnection
- Diaphragmatic breathing — 2 min
- Connection breath (exhale + PF lift + TVA draw) — 2 × 8
- Pelvic tilts supine — 2 × 10
- Glute squeezes — 2 × 10, 2-sec hold
- Supported child's pose — 60 sec
- Cat–cow — 2 × 8
- Side-lying thoracic openers — 1 × 6/side

### Walking
- Week 1: 10–15 min, 1–2×/day, flat
- Week 2: 15–25 min, 1–2×/day
- Stop if bleeding returns to red

### Scar
- Light fingertip contact around (not on) the scar. No mobilisation yet.

**End of phase check:** OB clearance at 6-week appointment + initial diastasis screen.

---

## PHASE 2 — Programme Weeks 3–4 (Postpartum Weeks 6–8)

**Focus:** Foundational bodyweight strength + deep core integration.
**Sessions:** 3–4×/week strength, 25–30 min + walking 20–30 min most days.

### Session A — Core & Posterior Chain
- Connection breath — 2 × 10
- Glute bridge — 3 × 10, slow tempo
- Heel slides — 2 × 8/side
- Dead bug, arms only — 2 × 8/side
- Bird-dog — 3 × 6/side
- Clamshells — 2 × 12/side
- Wall sit — 3 × 20 sec
- Side-lying leg lifts — 2 × 10/side

### Session B — Standing Strength & Posture
- Connection breath standing — 2 × 10
- Bodyweight squat to mat — 3 × 10
- Split stance hold — 2 × 20 sec/side
- Wall push-up — 3 × 8–10
- Standing hip hinge BW — 3 × 10
- Standing towel row (isometric) — 3 × 10
- Calf raises — 2 × 15
- Standing thoracic rotations — 2 × 8/side

### Session C — Mobility & Pelvic Floor
- 90/90 hip rocks — 2 × 6/side
- Happy baby — 60 sec
- Supported deep squat hold — 2 × 30 sec
- Quadruped rocking — 2 × 8
- Supine figure-4 — 45 sec/side
- Thread the needle — 2 × 5/side

### Cardio
- Walking 25–30 min, 5–6 days/week, Z1–low Z2
- Optional short low-impact circuit at end of one strength session

### Scar
- Daily mobilisation now permitted: pads of fingers, skin glide above/below/over, small circles, 2–3 min.

**End of phase check:** Diastasis re-screen. Confirm readiness gates before introducing load.

---

## PHASE 3 — Programme Weeks 5–6 (Postpartum Weeks 8–10) — INTENSIFIED

**Focus:** Real strength build. Light load introduced. Tempo and volume are the primary intensity levers.
**Sessions:** 4 strength + 1 conditioning/mobility, ~30–35 min strength sessions.

### Session A — Lower Body (Quad-Dominant)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goblet squat | 4 × 10 | 3-1-1-0 | 8–12 kg, RIR 3 |
| Reverse lunge | 3 × 8/side | 2-0-1-0 | BW or 2 × 4–6 kg |
| Bulgarian split squat | 3 × 8/side | 3-1-1-0 | BW |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 × 10/side | 2-2-1-0 | BW, 2-sec hold |
| Side plank (knees → feet) | 3 × 20 sec/side | — | — |
| Dead bug with light DB | 3 × 8/side | 3-0-3-0 | 2–4 kg |

### Session B — Upper Body
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| Push-up (incline → floor) | 4 × 6–10 | 3-1-1-0 | RIR 3 |
| Single-arm row, hinge | 4 × 10/side | 2-1-1-1 | 7–10 kg |
| Tall kneeling press | 3 × 10 | 2-0-1-1 | 2 × 4–6 kg |
| Bent-over reverse fly | 3 × 12 | 2-1-2-0 | 2 × 2–4 kg |
| Bear hold | 3 × 20 sec | — | BW |
| Pallof press (band) | 3 × 10/side | 2-2-1-0 | Moderate |

### Session C — Lower Body (Hinge-Dominant)
| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Tempo | Load |
|---|---|---|---|
| Romanian deadlift | 4 × 10 | 3-1-1-0 | 2 × 5–8 kg |
| Single-leg deadlift | 3 × 8/side | 3-0-1-0 | 1 × 5–8 kg |
| Step-up | 3 × 8/side | 2-0-1-0 | BW or 2 × 4–6 kg |
| Glute bridge with march | 3 × 10/side | 2-0-2-0 | BW or DB on hips |
| Bird-dog with hold | 3 × 8/side | 2-3-2-0 | 3-sec hold |
| Suitcase carry | 3 × 30 m | — | 1 × 8–12 kg |

### Session D — Upper + Core Density
**Week 5: straight sets. Week 6: circuit format.**
3 rounds, 45 sec on / 15 sec off, 90 sec between rounds:
- Push-up → Row (L) → Row (R) → Tall kneeling press → Dead bug → Side plank (alt sides per round)

### Session E — Conditioning + Mobility
- 25–35 min brisk walk with inclines
- 15 min mobility flow

### Cardio (Phase 3)
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Z2 walk 30–40 min |
| Wed | Z2 walk with hills 30–40 min |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk 20–30 min |
| Sat | 10-min low-impact circuit after Strength C |
| Sun | Long Z2 walk 45–60 min |

**Week 5:** RIR 4. **Week 6:** RIR 3, add 1–2 kg where Week 5 felt easy.

**End of phase check:** Diastasis re-screen. PF symptom check.

---

## PHASE 4 — Programme Weeks 7–9 (Postpartum Weeks 10–13)

**Focus:** Loaded strength endurance, walk-jog intervals if PF cleared, dynamic core prep.
**Sessions:** 4 strength + 2 cardio, 35–45 min strength sessions.

### Pelvic Floor Readiness Test (do at start of Phase 4)
10 heel raises → 10 jumping jacks in place → 1 min jog in place.
Watch for: leaking, heaviness, doming, pain.
**Pass** → proceed with walk-jog intervals.
**Fail** → stay on walking only, refer to pelvic health physio.

### Session A — Lower Body Strength
- Tempo squat (3-sec down): 4 × 10
- Reverse lunge with reach: 3 × 10/side
- Single-leg deadlift: 3 × 8/side, 1 × 5–8 kg
- Glute bridge march: 3 × 12/side
- Side plank from feet (or knees): 3 × 20 sec/side
- Dead bug with load: 3 × 8/side

### Session B — Upper Body Strength
- Push-up (incline → floor): 4 × 6–10
- Single-arm row: 3 × 10/side, 7–10 kg
- Pike push-up: 3 × 6
- Tall kneeling press: 3 × 10, 2 × 4–6 kg
- Bear crawl (slow): 3 × 4 lengths
- Hollow hold (knees bent): 3 × 15 sec

### Session C — Full Body Circuit
3 rounds, 40 sec work / 20 sec rest:
Squat → Push-up → Reverse lunge → Bird-dog → Glute bridge → Dead bug → Side plank

### Session D — Posterior Chain & Carries
- Romanian deadlift: 4 × 8, 2 × 8–10 kg
- Single-leg deadlift: 3 × 8/side, 1 × 8 kg
- Step-up: 3 × 8/side, 2 × 4–6 kg
- Suitcase carry: 3 × 30 m, 1 × 10–12 kg
- Pallof press: 3 × 10/side
- Bear hold: 3 × 20 sec

### Cardio (Phase 4)
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Walk-jog intervals: 5 min walk + 8 × (1 min jog / 2 min walk) + 5 min walk |
| Wed | Z2 walk with hills 40 min |
| Thu | 12-min low-impact conditioning circuit after Session B |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk 30 min |
| Sun | Long Z2 walk 60 min |

**Phase 4 load targets by week 9:**
- Goblet squat: 14–16 kg × 4 × 8
- RDL: 2 × 10–12 kg × 4 × 8
- Push-up: full × 3 × 6
- Suitcase carry: 14–16 kg × 30 m

**End of phase check:** Diastasis, PF symptoms, sleep/supply check.

---

## PHASE 5 — Programme Weeks 10–12 (Postpartum Weeks 13–16)

**Focus:** Strength expression. Density circuits. Light intervals. Cautious anterior core test.
**Sessions:** 4–5×/week, 40–45 min.

### Session A — Lower Body + Light Conditioning
- Squat (tempo or paused): 4 × 10
- Reverse lunge: 3 × 10/side
- Single-leg deadlift: 3 × 8/side
- Pogo hops (low, 2 inches): 3 × 20 sec — **only if PF asymptomatic**
- Lateral bounds (small): 3 × 6/side — same caveat
- Side plank with reach: 3 × 8/side

### Session B — Upper Body Strength
- Push-up: 4 × 8 (full or elevated as needed)
- Towel/DB row: 4 × 12
- Pike push-up: 3 × 8
- Tall kneeling press: 4 × 10
- Hollow hold: 3 × 20 sec
- Dead bug with load: 3 × 10/side

### Session C — Density Circuit (EMOM 20 min)
- Min 1: 10 squats
- Min 2: 8 push-ups
- Min 3: 10 reverse lunges (total)
- Min 4: 30 sec side plank (alternate sides each round)

### Session D — Posterior Chain & Core
- Single-leg glute bridge: 4 × 10/side
- Hip hinge / RDL: 4 × 10
- Bird-dog: 3 × 8/side
- Bear crawl: 3 × 6 lengths
- Dead bug: 3 × 10/side
- Side plank with hip dip: 3 × 8/side

### Session E — Walk / Yoga / Active Recovery

### Cardio (Phase 5)
| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| Mon | Continuous easy jog or walk-jog 25–35 min |
| Wed | Z2 walk with hills 45 min |
| Thu | Light intervals after Session B: 5 min easy + 6 × (30 sec Z3 / 90 sec easy) + 5 min easy |
| Fri | Z1 recovery walk 30 min |
| Sun | Long Z2 walk or jog/walk mix 60–75 min |

### Core — End-of-Programme Test
**Week 12:** if diastasis tests functional (gap ≤2 fingers, firm tension, no doming on head-lift), cautiously test a single set of slow tempo crunches (2 × 10, 3-sec up / 3-sec down). If clean and asymptomatic next day, this opens Phase 6 (week 13+).

---

## CORE PROGRESSION SUMMARY ACROSS 12 WEEKS

| Phase | Core Level | Key Exercises |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reconnection | Connection breath, pelvic tilts, glute squeezes |
| 2 | Anti-movement BW | Dead bug arms, bird-dog, glute bridge, side-lying lifts |
| 3 | Anti-movement loaded | Dead bug w/ DB, side plank, bird-dog hold, Pallof press, suitcase carry |
| 4 | Loaded anti-movement | Loaded dead bug, side plank from feet, bear crawl, farmer's carry |
| 5 | Dynamic core | Hollow hold, side plank w/ hip dip, renegade row (no push-up), test crunch at week 12 |

**No crunches, sit-ups, V-ups, Russian twists, or rotation under flexion in the 12 weeks.** These come in Week 13+ if diastasis screens functional.

---

## CARDIO PROGRESSION SUMMARY

| Phase | Weekly Cardio Volume | Intensity Ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.5–2.5 hrs walking | Z1 |
| 2 | 2–3 hrs walking | Z1–low Z2 |
| 3 | 3–4 hrs | Z2 + brief low Z3 in circuits |
| 4 | 3.5–4.5 hrs | Z3 (walk-jog) |
| 5 | 3.5–5 hrs | Z3 (continuous jog + light intervals) |

**No HIIT in this programme.** Earliest true HIIT consideration: month 6+ postpartum, gated by full PF + impact tolerance criteria.

---

## NUTRITION PLAN (Breastfeeding-Supportive)

### Daily Targets
- **Calories:** 2,400–2,600/day (maintenance + lactation)
- **Protein:** 125–155 g (1.8–2.2 g/kg)
- **Fat:** 55–70 g
- **Carbohydrate:** 280–340 g
- **Fibre:** 25–35 g
- **Fluid:** 3–3.5 L/day, more on cardio days

**Do not drop below ~1,800 kcal/day while breastfeeding.** Fat loss focus only post-supply-establishment, max 0.25–0.5 kg/week.

### Plate Template Every Meal
¼ protein (palm) + ¼ starch (cupped hand) + ½ veg/fruit + thumb of fat + fluid

### Meal Pattern
3 meals + 2–3 snacks. High-protein breakfast anchors the day. Bedside snack + water for night feeds.

### Priority Micronutrients
- Continue prenatal multivitamin
- Vitamin D 1,000–2,000 IU/
